text:
- If the appointment is for blood tests, it's really just for the blood draw and nothing else. Even though I mentioned I wanted to come back to update on my leg pain and that it hadn't improved, they told me to come back another day.
- I recommend coming at 10 am; there are fewer people and you won't have to wait long.
- The system is: Medical records > History taking > See doctor > Dispensing medication > Finance > Dispensing medication.
- If you come in the morning, there won't be enough parking. Drive a little further past the center; there's parking there, but it's always overflowing onto the street.

I recently had the opportunity to use this facility for the first time after recovering from COVID-19. After notifying the NHSO center about a change of healthcare provider under my universal health coverage scheme, they provided excellent guidance, as I had never used the scheme before. Following their instructions, the change was processed in less than half an hour, which was fantastic! I'd also like to commend the 1330 hotline; they were incredibly helpful.
On the day of my treatment, I called ahead to confirm my eligibility. The staff were very helpful and provided excellent guidance. They even took photos for my ATK test. Upon arrival at the health center, I simply informed the staff at the front desk, and they provided excellent service. The patient screening area was clearly separated, and the service from the examination to dispensing medication was superb. I highly recommend anyone with COVID-19 to see a doctor immediately, even if it's not severe, to ensure a faster recovery and prevent the spread of the virus.

There is parking available next to the building.

In summary, I was very impressed with my first experience using my universal health coverage at Public Health Center 65. Thank you very much to all the staff!

I came for dental treatment a week ago. They said they couldn't treat me and I needed to go to a hospital for treatment under my insurance, but they didn't provide a referral letter. Today I went to the hospital as instructed by the nurse, but they wouldn't accept me because I didn't have a referral letter. I wasted another day going back and forth.

The dentist who came at 3 PM was very rude. They just sat there laughing when I was in pain, which was really unacceptable. Even though I'm using my government health insurance, they shouldn't speak so disrespectfully. It might be normal for some people, but it's not the case with everyone.

The place was very clean, the staff provided excellent service, and the dentist on the 3rd floor was very gentle. The doctors and nurses were very kind and lovely. I was so excited I forgot to check the doctor's name.

text: All the staff here are wonderful. Public health has changed a lot now; people are very kind and compassionate. They aren't the cruel civil servants of the past. There are only kind and generous people who are willing to help. Thank you to all the staff at Center 65 for being kind to all citizens, regardless of wealth or poverty. Thank you so much.

Public Health Center No. 65, Bang Bon District
Provides medical check-ups, health care, family planning, dentistry, children's vaccinations, prenatal check-ups, etc. It's not crowded, so waiting times are short, and the service is good.
Phone numbers for inquiries: 02-4530-526, 02-4530-570
Open from 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM, with a lunch break.
However, currently it's open until 7:00 PM.
The staff provided excellent service, were attentive, gave good advice, and were polite and courteous.

I arrived for dental treatment at 3:00 PM. There were 4 people waiting to register, and a staff member from the center registered them. My relative tried to cut in front of the 4 people waiting and got the second spot in line. I reported in at 3:30 PM and had my dental work done at 4:00 PM. The doctor was very polite and gave excellent advice. The only issue was the staff handling the social security paperwork; they refused to provide a medical certificate, which wasted time when claiming the benefits. They should provide better guidance to patients to avoid unnecessary delays.
This is our first time getting dental work done here. We used our social security benefits for a filling, and the total cost was 600 baht. Is this price correct?

Overall, the staff's attitude was poor.

With us, the staff might have just been a bit curt. We contacted them to pick up a referral slip around 10-11 am but were unable to receive service. They said the queue was full and we had to come back at 4 pm because the staff hadn't had lunch yet and there were over a hundred people waiting.

I saw the staff yelling at other service users, especially scruffy-looking locals or delivery drivers.

I understand it's a free service, but it doesn't need to be this bad. In the end, we didn't wait because if we did, we probably wouldn't have time to use our hospital benefits anyway.

It's terrible. If the government is going to manage things this poorly, why not sell the benefits to a competent private hospital?
